newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower on last day of first half.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower on last day of first half.

text.p: Brazilian shares closed off for a third session in a row on profit-taking, helped by fund managers who sold stocks on the last day of the first half, brokers said.

The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 48 most traded shares ended 1.49 percent lower at 12,568 points. Market turnover was slightly lower at 929.9 million reais ($869.06 million), down from the recent daily average of over one billion reais.
The drop was widely expected as many domestic funds had bought heavily early last week ahead of the first half's close.
But traders do not expect the bout of profit-taking in the last three days of a spectacular first half to continue.
"As of tomorrow, we begin another game," said a senior trader.

He said the market will continue to move in tandem with the influx of money into local equity funds. Those funds have been the driving force behind the bolsa's rise, which in the first half reached 81.2 percent.
Analysts said, however, the bolsa could rise cautiously as investors stay guarded ahead of this week's U.S. FOMC meeting on interest rates.

Among the top gainers, government bank Banco do Brasil preferred jumped 5.74 percent to 12.90 reais.

Other bank stocks, however, fell. The voting stock of Banco Itau, which on Friday surged following its purchase of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, fell 1.03 percent to 480 reais. Itau's preferred stock dropped 2.11 percent to close at 603 reais.
